q-48385.solution:
First, we express

$$
f(x)=(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{@@N@@}.
$$

Now, we see that $f(x)$ can be expressed as the composite function

$$
f={u}^{@@N@@},\,u=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=@@K@@{u}^{@@M@@}\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-\operatorname{sin}⁡x.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =@@K@@{u}^{@@M@@}\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\  & =@@NK@@{u}^{@@M@@}\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\  & =@@NK@@(\operatorname{cos}⁡x)^{@@M@@}\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\  & =@@NK@@{cos}^{@@M@@}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=@@K@@u\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.

$$
